research.title: Somatic Evolution & Cancer
research.subtitle: Understanding cancer through evolutionary dynamics and clonal selection
research.overview: Cancer is fundamentally an evolutionary process occurring within the body. Our research applies evolutionary theory to understand tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and treatment resistance. By viewing cancer through an evolutionary lens, we develop new strategies for prediction and intervention.
areas: Clonal Evolution: Tracking the emergence and competition of cancer cell lineages within tumors using phylogenetic reconstruction
Mutation Accumulation: Modeling the temporal dynamics of somatic mutations and their fitness effects in cancer development
Treatment Resistance: Understanding how evolutionary processes drive resistance to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy
Tumor Heterogeneity: Characterizing spatial and temporal variation in tumor cell populations and its clinical implications
Metastatic Evolution: Investigating the evolutionary trajectories that enable cancer cells to colonize distant sites
research.methods: We integrate genomic data from single-cell sequencing, bulk tumor samples, and liquid biopsies with mathematical models of evolutionary dynamics. Our approaches include population genetics theory, stochastic simulation, and machine learning to predict tumor evolution and treatment outcomes.

projects.title: Adaptive Therapy Design
projects.description: Developing evolution-informed treatment strategies that exploit competitive interactions between resistant and sensitive cancer cells

projects.title: Early Detection Biomarkers
projects.description: Identifying evolutionary signatures in circulating tumor DNA for early cancer detection and monitoring

projects.title: Tumor Ecosystem Dynamics
projects.description: Modeling interactions between cancer cells, immune cells, and the tumor microenvironment as an evolving ecosystem

research.title: DNA/RNA Evolution & Phylogenetics
research.subtitle: Historical reconstruction and molecular evolution through computational phylogenetics
research.overview: Our DNA/RNA evolution research focuses on understanding the historical processes that have shaped genetic diversity across all domains of life. Using advanced phylogenetic methods, we reconstruct evolutionary relationships and infer the mechanisms driving molecular change.
areas: Phylogenetic Inference: Developing and applying maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods to reconstruct evolutionary trees from molecular sequence data
Molecular Clock Analysis: Estimating divergence times and rates of evolution across different lineages and genomic regions
RNA Structure Evolution: Investigating how RNA secondary and tertiary structures evolve under functional constraints
Codon Usage Bias: Analyzing selection pressures on synonymous codon usage and their implications for gene expression
Ancient DNA: Reconstructing evolutionary histories from degraded genetic material in paleontological and archaeological samples
research.methods: We employ cutting-edge computational methods including probabilistic models of sequence evolution, coalescent theory, and machine learning approaches to extract evolutionary signals from genomic data. Our work combines theoretical development with practical applications to biological questions.

projects.title: Viral RNA Evolution
projects.description: Tracking rapid evolutionary changes in RNA viruses to predict emergence of new variants

projects.title: Deep Time Phylogenomics
projects.description: Resolving ancient evolutionary relationships using whole-genome data and novel substitution models

projects.title: Functional Constraint Mapping
projects.description: Identifying regions of genomes under purifying selection through comparative genomics

research.title: Evolutionary Forecasting
research.subtitle: Leveraging evolutionary principles to forecast future states of large noisy systems
research.overview: Evolutionary forecasting applies principles from evolutionary theory to predict the future states of complex, dynamic systems. By treating systems as evolving populations subject to selection, drift, and mutation-like processes, we develop robust predictive models that account for uncertainty and adaptation in noisy environments.
areas: Adaptive Forecasting Models: Developing prediction frameworks that evolve with changing system dynamics and learn from forecast errors
Population-Level Predictions: Forecasting aggregate behaviors in large systems by modeling individual-level variation and selection pressures
Evolutionary Game Theory: Predicting strategic interactions and equilibria in competitive environments using evolutionary dynamics
Phylogenetic Forecasting: Using evolutionary relationships and historical patterns to predict future trait evolution and system trajectories
Noise-Robust Prediction: Developing forecasting methods that maintain accuracy despite high levels of stochasticity and measurement uncertainty
research.methods: We combine evolutionary algorithms, Bayesian inference, and machine learning to create forecasting systems that adapt to changing conditions. Our methods incorporate fitness landscapes, selection gradients, and evolutionary constraints to generate predictions that account for both deterministic trends and stochastic variation.

projects.title: Market Evolution Forecasting
projects.description: Predicting financial market dynamics by modeling trading strategies as evolving populations competing for resources

projects.title: Pathogen Trajectory Prediction
projects.description: Forecasting viral evolution and epidemic spread using phylodynamic models and evolutionary constraints

projects.title: Adaptive Climate Models
projects.description: Developing evolutionary forecasting approaches for ecological systems responding to environmental change

research.title: Immunity
research.subtitle: Evolutionary perspectives on immune system function and host defense
research.overview: The immune system is a product of millions of years of coevolution with pathogens. Our research examines how evolutionary pressures have shaped immune function, diversity, and dysfunction. We study both the evolution of immunity across species and the rapid evolution occurring within individual immune responses.
areas: Adaptive Immune Diversity: Understanding how somatic evolution generates antibody and T-cell receptor diversity through V(D)J recombination and somatic hypermutation
Host-Pathogen Arms Races: Investigating the coevolutionary dynamics between immune defenses and pathogen evasion strategies
Immune System Evolution: Comparing immune mechanisms across species to understand the evolutionary origins and constraints of immunity
Autoimmunity and Trade-offs: Examining how evolutionary trade-offs between pathogen defense and self-tolerance lead to autoimmune diseases
Clonal Selection Dynamics: Modeling the evolutionary dynamics of lymphocyte populations during immune responses and immunological memory formation
research.methods: We use immune repertoire sequencing to track the evolution of B and T cell populations, comparative genomics to understand immune system evolution across species, and mathematical modeling to predict immune response dynamics. Our work integrates immunology with evolutionary theory and population genetics.

projects.title: Vaccine Response Evolution
projects.description: Tracking the evolutionary dynamics of antibody responses to vaccination and predicting long-term immunity

projects.title: Cancer Immunoediting
projects.description: Understanding how tumors evolve to escape immune surveillance and how to leverage evolutionary principles for immunotherapy

projects.title: Innate Immunity Evolution
projects.description: Investigating the evolutionary conservation and diversification of pattern recognition receptors across species

research.title: Evolution of Financial Markets
research.subtitle: Applying evolutionary theory to economic systems and market dynamics
research.overview: Financial markets exhibit evolutionary dynamics analogous to biological systems, with competing strategies, adaptation to changing environments, and selection pressures shaping market behavior. Our research applies evolutionary theory and population dynamics to understand and predict financial market phenomena.
areas: Trading Strategy Evolution: Modeling how investment strategies compete, adapt, and evolve in response to market conditions and other strategies
Market Ecology: Analyzing financial markets as ecosystems with diverse agent types, resource competition, and predator-prey dynamics
Innovation Diffusion: Studying how financial innovations spread through markets and the evolutionary pressures that shape their adoption
Regulatory Evolution: Understanding how market regulations coevolve with trading practices and institutional structures
Crisis Dynamics: Applying evolutionary models to understand market crashes, bubbles, and systemic risk emergence
research.methods: We employ agent-based modeling, evolutionary game theory, and network analysis to simulate market evolution. Our work integrates high-frequency trading data with theoretical models from population genetics and ecology to reveal fundamental principles governing market dynamics.

projects.title: Algorithmic Trading Evolution
projects.description: Investigating how machine learning algorithms evolve and compete in modern high-frequency trading environments

projects.title: Cryptocurrency Market Dynamics
projects.description: Applying evolutionary models to understand the emergence and competition of digital currencies and DeFi protocols

projects.title: Behavioral Finance Evolution
projects.description: Modeling how cognitive biases and heuristics evolve under market selection pressures

research.title: Microbes
research.subtitle: Evolutionary dynamics of microbial populations and communities
research.overview: Microbial evolution operates at extraordinary speeds, making microbes ideal systems for studying evolutionary processes in real-time. Our research examines how bacteria, archaea, viruses, and fungi evolve in response to environmental pressures, competition, and cooperation within complex communities.
areas: Experimental Evolution: Using laboratory evolution experiments to observe adaptation, mutation accumulation, and evolutionary innovation in real-time
Microbial Community Dynamics: Modeling ecological and evolutionary interactions within microbiomes and their impact on host health
Horizontal Gene Transfer: Investigating how genetic exchange between microbes accelerates adaptation and spreads traits like antibiotic resistance
Metabolic Evolution: Understanding how microbial metabolic networks evolve to exploit new resources and environmental niches
Viral-Host Coevolution: Studying the evolutionary arms race between bacteriophages and their bacterial hosts
research.methods: We combine experimental evolution with high-throughput genomic sequencing, metagenomics, and computational modeling. Our work integrates population genetics theory with systems biology to predict evolutionary trajectories and understand the genetic basis of adaptation.

projects.title: Antibiotic Resistance Evolution
projects.description: Tracking the emergence and spread of resistance mechanisms in bacterial populations under different treatment regimens

projects.title: Microbiome Assembly Rules
projects.description: Determining how evolutionary and ecological processes shape the composition and function of microbial communities

projects.title: Synthetic Microbial Consortia
projects.description: Engineering stable microbial communities for biotechnology applications using evolutionary principles

risk_research.title: Evolutionary Targets of Concern
risk_research.description: Identifying specific evolutionary trajectories, mutations, or gene combinations that would create heightened biosecurity risks and developing early warning systems.

risk_context.overview: Synthetic biology enables the design and construction of new biological parts, devices, and systems for useful purposes. However, these capabilities raise important biosecurity considerations that require rigorous mathematical and theoretical frameworks.

keyConcepts.definition: Strategies to prevent engineered organisms from persisting in unintended environments, including genetic, chemical, and physical barriers.
Genetic circuits designed to eliminate cells when specific conditions are met or when they escape containment, using toxin-antitoxin systems or essential gene dependencies.
The capacity of engineered genetic circuits to resist degradation or escape through mutation and selection over microbial generations.
Engineering organisms to require specific nutrients not available in natural environments, creating a metabolic dependency for survival.
Genetic elements that bias inheritance to increase their frequency in populations, with potential for rapid ecological spread.

currentChallenges: Traditional homology-based DNA screening is inadequate for generative AI-designed proteins with novel functions
Synthetic gene circuits often degrade over time due to mutation and selection pressures from host resource burden
Horizontal gene transfer can spread engineered genetic elements to non-target organisms
Long-term evolutionary dynamics of engineered systems remain poorly characterized
Risk assessment frameworks lag behind the pace of technological advancement

research.subtitle: Advancing biosecurity through mathematical frameworks and evolutionary prediction

synbio.title: Synthetic Biology Context
synbio.description: Synthetic biology enables precise engineering of biological systems, from modified bacteria to entirely novel organisms. While this field holds immense promise for medicine, agriculture, and environmental remediation, it also presents unique biosecurity challenges. Our research addresses the critical gap between engineered intent and evolutionary reality, developing mathematical frameworks to predict and prevent unintended consequences.
synbio.challenge1: Evolutionary escape from designed containment systems

containment.title: Predictive Containment Frameworks
containment.description: We develop mathematical models to establish scientifically grounded expiration dates for containment measures. Our frameworks integrate mutation rates, selection pressures, and population dynamics to predict when engineered safeguards may fail.

killSwitch.title: Kill-Switch Evolution
killSwitch.description: Bacterial kill-switches are designed to eliminate engineered organisms outside controlled environments. However, evolutionary pressure can lead to escape mutants. Our research predicts mutation pathways and designs evolution-resistant safety mechanisms.
killSwitch.focus1: Mutation rate analysis in safety circuits

spillover.title: Spillover Risk Assessment
spillover.description: We quantify the probability and impact of engineered organisms interacting with natural ecosystems or immune systems. Our models integrate ecological theory, immunology, and evolutionary genetics.

interaction.title: Interaction Risk Modeling
interaction.description: Complex interactions between engineered organisms and their environment can produce unexpected outcomes. We model immunological responses, ecological competition, and metabolic cross-talk.

targets.title: Evolutionary Targets of Concern
targets.description: Certain evolutionary pathways pose heightened biosecurity risks. We identify and monitor specific genetic targets that could lead to containment failure or increased virulence.

synbio.title: Contexto de Biología Sintética
synbio.description: La biología sintética permite la ingeniería precisa de sistemas biológicos, desde bacterias modificadas hasta organismos completamente novedosos. Si bien este campo tiene un enorme potencial para la medicina, la agricultura y la remediación ambiental, también presenta desafíos únicos de bioseguridad. Nuestra investigación aborda la brecha crítica entre la intención diseñada y la realidad evolutiva, desarrollando marcos matemáticos para predecir y prevenir consecuencias no deseadas.

synbio.title: Contexto de Biologia Sintética
synbio.description: A biologia sintética permite a engenharia precisa de sistemas biológicos, desde bactérias modificadas até organismos completamente novos. Embora este campo tenha um enorme potencial para medicina, agricultura e remediação ambiental, também apresenta desafios únicos de biossegurança. Nossa pesquisa aborda a lacuna crítica entre intenção projetada e realidade evolutiva, desenvolvendo estruturas matemáticas para prever e prevenir consequências não intencionais.
synbio.challenge1: Escape evolutivo de sistemas de contenção projetados
synbio.challenge2: Transferência de genes para organismos naturais
synbio.challenge4: Estabilidade a longo prazo de características projetadas

containment.title: Estruturas de Contenção Preditivas
containment.description: Desenvolvemos modelos matemáticos para estabelecer datas de expiração cientificamente fundamentadas para medidas de contenção. Nossas estruturas integram taxas de mutação, pressões de seleção e dinâmicas populacionais para prever quando as salvaguardas projetadas podem falhar.
containment.approach2: Otimização de contenção de múltiplas barreiras
containment.approach3: Algoritmos de avaliação de risco temporal

killSwitch.title: Evolução de Interruptores de Segurança
killSwitch.description: Interruptores de segurança bacterianos são projetados para eliminar organismos projetados fora de ambientes controlados. No entanto, pressão evolutiva pode levar a mutantes de escape. Nossa pesquisa prevê vias de mutação e projeta mecanismos de segurança resistentes à evolução.
killSwitch.focus1: Análise de taxa de mutação em circuitos de segurança
killSwitch.focus3: Arquitetura de interruptores de segurança redundantes
